description: Trigger evals: queries that should and should not activate build-companion.
positive: Which piece do I cut first for the cubby bench?
Walk me through the glue-up and squaring.
How do I keep the three openings equal without measuring each one?
My first opening came out 10.5 instead of 11 — what now?
The shelf won't drop between the sides; did I cut something wrong?
What's my dry-fit check before I fasten the top?
Is this finished bench a two-person lift?
negative: Design a 4-ft version of this bench.
Render the build guide HTML for this project.
Does this cut list close before I start?
Confirm which saw I actually own.
I finished the benches — update the shop inventory and lessons.
notes: Positives are all at-the-bench execution: cut order, layout technique, dry-fit, deviation recovery, safety. Negatives belong to build-planner (design), guide-renderer (static guides), cut-verifier (pre-build number check), shop-inventory (tool confirmation), or shop-close-out (post-build update). The deviation cases ('10.5 not 11') are build-companion's because they are live at-the-bench recovery; cut-verifier is the math engine it delegates to, not the trigger.
